paragraphs.en: When classrooms closed during the pandemic, schools moved online almost overnight. The experience taught a hard lesson: technology can deliver lessons, but it cannot easily replace the human core of education.
paragraphs.zh: 疫情期间教室关闭时，学校几乎一夜之间转到了线上。这段经历给了人一个深刻的教训：技术可以传递课程内容，却难以替代教育的人文内核。

paragraphs.en: Many children fell behind, and the pattern was painfully familiar. Students from poorer homes, with weaker internet and less parental support, lost far more ground than their better-off classmates.
paragraphs.zh: 许多孩子掉了队，而这其中的模式令人心酸地熟悉：家境较差的学生——网络更差、家长支持更少——比条件优越的同学落后得更多。

paragraphs.en: Teachers, too, discovered what online learning does well and where it fails. Recorded lectures suit review, but children need live interaction, feedback and encouragement to stay motivated.
paragraphs.zh: 教师们也发现了线上学习擅长什么、又在何处失灵。录播课适合复习，但孩子需要实时的互动、反馈和鼓励才能保持学习动力。

paragraphs.en: The challenge now is to keep what worked while repairing what was damaged. Schools are introducing tutoring programmes, smaller groups and extra hours for the subjects hit hardest by closure.
paragraphs.zh: 现在的挑战是保留行之有效的做法，同时修复受损的部分。各学校正在引入补习计划、小组教学和针对受停课影响最大学科的额外课时。

paragraphs.en: There is also an opportunity. Digital tools can free teachers from marking and administration, giving them more time for the conversations that really shape young minds.
paragraphs.zh: 这里也存在机遇。数字工具可以把教师从批改和管理事务中解放出来，让他们有更多时间进行真正塑造年轻心灵的对话。

paragraphs.en: Education systems that treat the last two years as a gap to be filled, rather than a change to be understood, will repeat the same mistakes. The screen is a tool, not a teacher.
paragraphs.zh: 如果教育体系把这过去两年仅仅当作需要填补的空缺，而不是需要理解的变革，就会重蹈覆辙。屏幕是工具，不是教师。
